summary:
We built 6Dimensions Lunar Landing Site Navigator, an interactive 3D exploration and decision-making tool that lets users experience and compare four candidate Artemis landing sites near the Moon's south pole.

Using real NASA terrain data and a 15-year astronomical almanac, our platform recreates the lunar landscape and visualizes the Sun, Earth, and local horizon at each site. Users can watch sunlight sweep across crater rims, see Earth above the horizon, and track live countdowns to the next sunrise or sunset.

Our comparison dashboard evaluates four critical factors for a sustainable lunar presence: solar power, Earth communication, terrain hazards, and proximity to potential water ice. Connecting Ridge receives sunlight 88.9% of the time, while Malapert Massif offers 84.8% Earth visibility. Neither wins every category, revealing why landing-site selection requires balancing competing priorities.

Beyond the data, users can freely explore the terrain, drive a solar-powered rover, and inspect the Gateway station in lunar orbit.

6Dimensions transforms complex lunar datasets into an immersive experience, helping users understand the challenges of establishing humanity's long-term presence on the Moon.
details:
Long Video Version: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YyHuiSfoENXRvjPY3IIoBUSgYCj1hYq_/view?usp=drive_link

6Dimensions Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive 3D platform designed to help users explore, evaluate, and compare four potential landing sites near the Moon's south pole.

Our platform combines NASA lunar terrain data with a 15-year astronomical almanac to reconstruct the environment at each candidate site. Users can select a location, explore its terrain in 3D, and observe the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the local horizon.

The system calculates and visualizes solar illumination, Earth visibility, terrain obstruction, and upcoming sunrise and sunset events. A comparison dashboard presents key metrics, including illumination percentage, Earth communication availability, and longest continuous lunar night.

Selecting a lunar landing site is not simply about finding the flattest terrain. A sustainable lunar base requires sufficient sunlight for power, reliable communication with Earth, manageable terrain hazards, and access to potential water-ice resources.

Our analysis highlights these competing priorities. Connecting Ridge achieves 88.9% solar illumination, making it attractive for solar power. Malapert Massif provides 84.8% Earth visibility, offering advantages for direct communication. However, no single location performs best across every criterion.

By presenting these differences in both quantitative comparisons and immersive visualizations, our platform allows users to understand why mission planners must balance multiple environmental constraints.

Beyond numerical analysis, 6Dimensions offers three ways to experience the lunar environment.

Free Flight: Navigate freely above realistic lunar terrain to investigate crater rims, slopes, and surrounding geography.

Rover Exploration: Drive a solar-powered rover across the landscape to experience the terrain from a surface-level perspective.

Gateway Visualization: Inspect the Gateway relay station in its modeled lunar orbit and explore its relationship to future lunar operations.

Our project's central innovation is connecting scientific analysis with interactive exploration. Traditional landing-site studies often rely on maps, charts, and numerical datasets. We bring these elements together in an accessible 3D environment, allowing users to experience the same geographic and astronomical constraints represented in the data.

The changing positions of the Sun and Earth make abstract engineering challenges immediately understandable. Users can see how crater walls obstruct sunlight or communication and why even a relatively favorable site may experience operational limitations.

6Dimensions aims to make lunar exploration more accessible to students, educators, space enthusiasts, and anyone interested in humanity's return to the Moon.

By combining NASA scientific data, interactive simulations, and side-by-side comparisons, our platform encourages evidence-based decision-making while making complex space science engaging and intuitive.

Ultimately, 6Dimensions turns the question of where humanity should land on the Moon into something users can explore, visualize, and investigate themselves.
